课程简介（中文）

本课程旨在引导学生全面理解学术论文写作的核心要素，以及研究与撰写的完整过程。课程致力于培养学生成为“语言侦探”，通过利用各类数字资源，掌握提升学术写作水平的工具、知识与技能。学生将学习如何开展严谨的学术研究，并运用规范的学术格式清晰地表达自己的观点。本学期所积累的知识与能力，最终将凝结为一篇由学生自选主题的学术论文。

课程简介（英文）

The course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the essential qualities of research paper writing, as well as the research and composition process. It aims to equip students with the tools, knowledge, and skills to become a “language detective” by using digital resources to enhance their academic writing. Students will learn to conduct rigorous academic research and to express their ideas clearly in an academic format. The semester's accumulation of knowledge will culminate in an academic paper on a topic of their choice.

教学目标

 By the end of this term, students should have an increased awareness of the key features of research paper writing, and they should be able to:

  • analyze and apply genre conventions
  • understand the structure and rhetoric of academic research papers
  • search for, evaluate, and integrate sources effectively
  • improve academic language and phrasing using corpora
  • write and revise different sections of a research paper
  • revise and edit research papers effectively
  • prevent plagiarism and uphold academic integrity
  • develop independent research and writing skills

教学方式

This course employs a blend of top-down genre analysis and bottom-up data-driven learning, providing students with both a conceptual understanding of research writing and practical tools for improving their academic language. The teaching methods are designed to engage students actively with both the structure and language of research papers, with a focus on hands-on practice, feedback, and self-reflection.

Top-Down Genre Analysis:

Approach: Each week, students will engage in genre analysis, examining the structure, features, and rhetorical moves of academic research papers from their field. This top-down approach helps students understand the conventions and expectations of academic writing in their discipline.

Activities: Students will work with sample texts, annotating sections (e.g., introductions, literature reviews, methods) to identify key rhetorical moves and strategies. Group discussions and presentations will help students collaboratively analyze and compare different research papers, fostering a deeper understanding of how genres function in academic contexts.

Bottom-Up Data-Driven Learning:

Approach: A core aspect of the course is improving academic writing through corpus-based analysis. This bottom-up approach uses real-world data from academic corpora to examine language patterns, phrases, and grammatical structures.

Activities: Students will engage with corpora (e.g., COCA, BAWE) to explore discipline-specific vocabulary, collocations, hedging devices, and academic syntax. They will use corpus tools to find examples of common academic phrases, compare language use across genres, and apply this knowledge to revise their own writing. This approach helps students refine their academic style and avoid common language errors.

Task-Based Learning:

Approach: The course includes task-based activities where students apply their knowledge of genre conventions, rhetorical moves, and academic language to produce their own research papers. These tasks are designed to mirror real-world academic writing tasks, such as drafting sections of a research paper, revising using corpus data, and engaging in self-reflection.

Activities: Tasks include writing a research introduction, synthesizing sources in a literature review, drafting methods and results sections, and revising drafts. Each task is aligned with course objectives and builds toward the final research paper submission.

Individualized Support and Reflection:

Approach: Throughout the course, individualized feedback will be provided through regular writing assignments, peer reviews, and in-class activities. This feedback will be tailored to each student’s progress and areas of need. Self-reflection will also play a key role, as students will reflect on their writing development and how they’ve applied corpus insights and peer feedback to improve their drafts.

Activities: Students will submit draft versions of their papers at various stages, receiving personalized feedback from both the instructor and peers. They will also keep a reflective journal where they evaluate their own writing progress and note how they have incorporated feedback into subsequent revisions.

教学内容与进度安排

教学内容安排 （具体到每节课内容，明确每节课要达到的教学目标）：

 

 

Section I: Developing Genre Awareness (Weeks 1-2)

Week 1

 

Course Introduction and Overview

Content: Introduction to course objectives, expectations, and assessment methods. Overview of academic genres and their significance in research writing.

Goals: Familiarize students with the course structure and goals; introduce the concept of genre and academic conventions in research writing.

Tasks:

l  Discuss the features of academic research papers across disciplines.

l  Complete a diagnostic activity where students identify sections in sample articles.

Week 2

 

Recognizing Genre-Specific Features in Research Articles

Content: Analyze research articles from students’ fields to identify standard structures, organization, and stylistic features.

Goals: Recognize discipline-specific expectations and typical structures of research papers; build foundational knowledge of genre features.

Tasks:

l  Annotate a research article to label different sections and identify academic tone.

l  Write a short reflection comparing the structures of research papers in two fields.

 

Section II: Understanding Rhetorical Sections and Moves (Weeks 3-7)

Week 3

 

Online

Understanding a Research Report and Searching for Sources

Content: Overview of the structure of a full research report (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion); introduction to strategies for finding and evaluating academic sources.

Goals: Recognize the purpose and function of each research report section; develop skills for locating and assessing credible academic sources related to their topics.

Tasks:

l  Analyze a sample research report, annotating each section to understand its purpose and common features.

l  Use academic databases to search for sources, complete a source evaluation worksheet, and briefly summarize how each source relates to their research questions.

Week 4

 

Introduction and Literature Review: Rhetorical Moves

Content: Introduction to rhetorical moves in the introduction (e.g., Swales’ CARS model) and literature review sections. Emphasis on setting context, establishing a research gap, and synthesizing sources.

Goals: Identify key moves for framing research questions and establishing background; practice synthesizing literature to set up the research context.

Tasks:

l  Identify and label rhetorical moves in the introduction and literature review of a sample article.

l  Write a draft introductory paragraph using at least two CARS moves; create a synthesis paragraph comparing two sources.

Week 5

 

Online

Methods Section: Structuring, Describing Procedures, and Plagiarism Prevention

Content: This week focuses on the structure and clarity required in the Methods section, including the importance of transparency in describing research procedures. Students will also learn about plagiarism prevention, focusing on how to ethically attribute sources when discussing research methods, tools, and techniques.

Goals:

Understand the role and structure of the Methods section in a research paper.

Practice clear and precise description of research methods, procedures, and instruments.

Learn how to ethically attribute sources of methods, tools, and concepts to avoid plagiarism.

Tasks:

l  Analyze a sample Methods section, paying attention to how procedures are described and how external sources are cited.

l  Write a draft Methods section for a hypothetical study in their field, incorporating citations for any external methods or techniques referenced. Emphasize clear description and proper attribution.

l  Task 3: Participate in a brief class discussion on plagiarism prevention, focusing on common mistakes in the Methods section (e.g., failing to cite specific research instruments or previous studies). Discuss how to properly paraphrase, quote, and cite when discussing methodology.

Week 6

 

Results Section: Presenting Data Clearly

Content: Focus on the conventions of reporting data objectively in the results section; emphasis on clarity, conciseness, and the use of visuals (tables/figures).

Goals: Develop skills for organizing and presenting results; understand how to integrate visuals into text appropriately.

Tasks:

l  Outline a results section for a set of sample data.

l  Write sample sentences that describe data trends objectively and clearly.

Week 7

 

Online

Discussion and Conclusion: Interpreting Results and Making Implications

Content: Identifying rhetorical moves in the discussion and conclusion sections, including interpreting findings, discussing implications, and suggesting future research directions.

Goals: Learn to craft insightful discussions that interpret results and highlight their significance; practice drawing conclusions and suggesting follow-up studies.

Tasks:

l  Annotate a discussion section to identify interpretation and implication moves.

l  Write a draft discussion paragraph, interpreting hypothetical results and suggesting implications.

Week 8

Midterm presentation day

 

Section III: Improving Phrasing and Grammar with Corpora (Weeks 9-11)

Week 9

 

Introduction to Corpora for Academic Phrasing

Content: Introduction to corpus tools for finding field-specific collocations and phrases.

Goals: Use corpus tools to identify accurate academic phrasing.

Tasks:

l  Search for collocations (e.g., “significant increase”) and record findings.

l  Replace informal phrases in a sample paragraph using corpus-sourced phrases.

Week 10

 

Online

Enhancing Grammar with Corpora

Content: Using corpora to observe grammar patterns (hedging, tense) and correct errors.

Goals: Improve grammatical accuracy in academic writing.

Tasks:

l  Analyze sentences for hedging language using a corpus.

l  Rewrite sentences for grammatical accuracy and academic tone.

Week 11

 

Corpus Practice and Consolidation

Content: Reinforcing corpus use; guided practice with field-specific phrases and structures.

Goals: Gain confidence in using corpus tools independently.

Tasks:

l  Compile frequently-used academic phrases from corpus findings.

l  Complete a peer review exercise, offering feedback based on corpus evidence.

 

Section IV: Editing and Revising with Corpora (Weeks 11-14)

Week 12

 

Online

Self-Editing Techniques Using Corpora

Content: Using corpora for self-editing, including checking word choice, transitions, and conciseness.

Goals: Develop self-editing skills to improve language accuracy and style.

Tasks:

l  Identify and replace overused words with alternatives from corpus findings.

l  Edit a draft focusing on coherence and smooth transitions.

Week 13

 

Revision and Final Draft Preparation

Content: Final revisions with focus on coherence, accuracy, and genre conventions.

Goals: Prepare a polished final draft.

Tasks:

l  Use a revision checklist for the final draft.

l  Incorporate self-editing and peer feedback.

Week 14

 

Online

Final Paper Submission and Course Reflection

Content: Submit the final paper and reflect on learning progress.

Goals: Conclude the course with a reflective analysis of skills developed.

Tasks:

l  Write a reflection on how corpus tools and genre analysis improved your writing.

l  Share one key takeaway from the course in a class discussion.

Week 15

 

Final presentation day

Week 16

 

Q & A
